questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I originally wanted to go to Australia but because of corona this was not possible. I researched my opportunities for exchange in Europe and found Wageningen University and Research in the Netherlands. I was very impressed of the pictures of the campus with a lot of modern buildings and plants. Furthermore, it was described as a very international university with one of the best ratings among life sciences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Mails were sent and I was immediately assigned to a buddy program which is part of the AID where I got to learn to know people from abroad and from the Netherlands. We were assigned to two mentors who showed us campus, the city and who were open for questions. We went to do activities together both planned from the university and planned from the mentors.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from my buddy mentors and I could always write to the exchange coordinator from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
There is the possibility of signing in on
room.nl
for a small fee which I can really recommend. Here there is a lot of student housing close to campus which is affordable. This should be done as soon as possible as you will be higher prioritized then. A month before the start of the semester international students are prioritized which makes it easier to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Wageningen is very small so off campus is not far away from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There was always a mail which is sent in advance to remind of the course registration which was nice.
It was also often possible to change courses if there was enough space in the course and if it was granted of the course coordinator

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Course registration is done through a platform called
osiris.nl
where you can read a small course description, a description of the exam and what is expected of you as a student. This is also where you sign up for courses. It was quite straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator could always be contacted if there were problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the courses I wanted. I signed up from the beginning for the whole exchange period and was put on waiting lists for several of them. When the next period came closer I was accepted to the course. Some courses are mandatory for people of specific studies so these may be difficult to join, but if you sing up early it should be possible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I can reccomend the Genomics couse.
I cannot recommend the Plant biotechnology course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the exam matched what was tought in the course. Also all the courses start off by explaining very trivial material as it is supposed to be possible to follow courses from all types of studies.
However, the exam for the course Plant biotechnology did not match what was tought in the lectures and during the practicals. The level of the exam was much too high and covered subjects not covered in the lectures. More than half of the students failed this course. I do not recommend it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The days are much longer than at KU and sometimes I had classes from 8 in the morning til 18.
However, there is almost always a 2h break in the middle of the day to meet up with friends or do sports.
The long days also meant that the weekends were mostly free to be used for parties, meeting with friends or traveling.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genetic Analysis Trends and Concepts
Introduction to bioinformatics
Plant biotechnology
Genomics
Plants and Health 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Genetic Analysis Trends and Concepts - it was really interesting with a lot of lab work regarding genetic traits and enthusiastic teachers.
Genomics - it was a nice introduction to bioinformatics and the teacher was really nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Router had to be bought

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food was much less expensive than in Denmark. Also all the stores and supermarkets were much cheaper.
Public transport was very expensive. If you have a personal OV card it gets cheaper though. Then you have to have a dutch bank account.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different associations which I could join, who organized a lot of social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Especially the international organisations ESN and ISOW are good to join as an exchange student to get to know other people.
Also, really nice sports facilities were available for a cheap fee.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit the market and the Rijn.
Go traveling.
Go to parties at the international club and house parties.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy as dutch culture is very similar to danish culture.
Dutch people are much more open than danish people which makes it easier to socialize with them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socialising with the dutchies is possible at group work or at house parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not really cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Dutch people are very open to meeting new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Say yes to all the opportunities especially at the beginning.
It can be really overwhelming but I think you get used to being social and you learn a lot from it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people and traveling a lot. The Netherlands is a very nice country with beautiful nature and it is located very central in Europe so it is easy to visit all the neighboring contries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Failing a course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
